title: Milloin: answering with weekdays
summary: For on a named weekday, use the essive ending -na/-nä. Milloin sinä tulet? — Tulen maanantaina.
prerequisiteSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
objectives: Ask which weekday an event happens on with milloin.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
For on a named weekday, use the essive ending -na/-nä. This ending marks the day of the event: maanantai + na gives maanantaina (“on Monday”). The question still begins with milloin.
keyPoints: Milloin asks for the event's time, not the day word's dictionary form.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Use the complete weekday form after the supplied verb: Tulen tiistaina (“I am coming on Tuesday”). A short reply Tiistaina is natural. The ordinary weekday names in this lesson all take -na; do not add an English-style preposition.
A natural short reply to “Milloin sinä tulet?” is “Maanantaina.” (“On Monday.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
Weekday time expressions retain -na in this negative correction. The second sentence identifies the actual day rather than leaving milloin unanswered.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the taught weekday + -na form for on that day.

tiistaina means on Tuesday here. Tiistai + -na gives tiistaina.
keskiviikkona means on Wednesday here. Keskiviikko retains kk before -na: keskiviikkona.
torstaina means on Thursday here. Torstai + -na gives torstaina.
perjantaina means on Friday here. Perjantai + -na gives perjantaina.
lauantaina means on Saturday here. Lauantai + -na gives lauantaina.
sunnuntaina means on Sunday here. Sunnuntai + -na gives sunnuntaina.

examples.english: I am not coming on Monday. I am coming on Tuesday.
steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
tule: come; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.
